// why: Type-checking only — this project is plain JavaScript and stays that way.
`checkJs` is what turns src/db/shim.d.ts into a gate over all 46 files:
a missed await on a shim call becomes 'Property map does not exist on
type Promise<Row[]>' at build time rather than a truthy Promise at runtime.
`strict` is off deliberately. Turning it on across a codebase that was
never written for it produces thousands of unrelated nullability errors,
which would bury the one class this gate exists to surface. It can be
raised per-file later; the await class does not need it.
The harnesses are INCLUDED, and that is not tidiness. The gate used to stop
at src/, so converting an engine turned every e2e-*.js that drives it into a
missed-await site the gate could not see — and the harness is where the
coverage lives, so the conversion's own verification is what breaks first,
looking like a regression in the engine. Measured: converting the four small
engines left eleven un-awaited call sites across three harnesses, all
invisible here. Including them costs advisory noise (counted, not gated).
It closes most of that frontier, not all of it, and the remainder is worth
knowing: a DISCARDED promise — `retention.pruneLogs(now());` as a bare
statement — reads no property off anything, so no type system can see it.
Measured: re-dropping that await leaves this gate silent while the harness
itself goes from 23/23 to 15/23. The layers do different jobs; this one
catches a Promise being USED, and only a run catches one being ignored.
